**1B.8 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is **mostly negative** for crisis de-escalation and accidental-war prevention. I found one weak restraint signal in May, but the stronger pattern is tactical-nuclear signaling, doctrinal hardening, and sustained readiness posture. I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Putin preserved crisis channels in a way that clearly reduced accidental-war risk.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 1B.8 | `Answers by Vladimir Putin and Alexander Lukashenko to media questions` | President of Russia | 2024-05-09 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002 | Putin said a tactical nuclear drill was “not about using these weapons” and “just routine work.” This is the clearest de-escalatory phrasing I found in 2024, but it was limited to a live nuclear exercise in Belarus and did not amount to broader crisis de-escalation. | 1B.8, 1B.2, 1B.1 |
| Slightly for 1B.8 | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, respond to alarm activations in weapons-storage areas, and specify actions for nuclear, chemical, and biological attack scenarios. This improves procedural discipline and accident response, but it is only indirect evidence for crisis de-escalation. | 1B.8, 1B.3, 1B.7 |
| Against 1B.8 | `Russia to practice tactical nuclear weapon scenario to deter West` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-practice-tactical-nuclear-weapon-scenario-to-deter-west--defence-ministry-3419973 | Russia announced tactical nuclear drills framed as deterrence against the West. That is crisis signaling, not calm communication; it increases the chance that adversaries read the situation as escalatory. | 1B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Against 1B.8 | `Russia will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Reuters reported that Moscow justified the doctrine revision as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. This is clear coercive signaling in a live crisis, not preservation of deconfliction channels. | 1B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.5 |
| Against 1B.8 | `Expanded meeting of the Ministry of Defence board` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/75887 | Putin said Russia had specified nuclear-use principles, kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert, and continued exercises while linking posture to U.S. missile deployments. That is sustained escalatory messaging, not crisis de-escalation or accident-risk reduction. | 1B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.5 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported conclusion: **No**. Putin did not consistently de-escalate or preserve crisis channels in 2024.
- The only positive evidence is a **narrow, exercise-specific disclaimer** in May and a **procedural safety** decree in March.
- The broader pattern is **escalatory**: tactical nuclear drills, doctrine revision justified by the Ukraine war, and continued constant-alert rhetoric.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of a clearly preserved U.S./NATO deconfliction channel, hotline reassurance, or other public crisis-communication move that would materially lower accidental-war risk.
